paragraphs.source_en: Nothing in the world reflects a commander’s disposition more clearly than the character of his soldiers. From the day he was born, Oda Nobunaga had been a once-in-an-age genius who delighted in astonishing others and repeatedly succeeded in doing so. But what would happen if retainers several degrees smaller in capacity than Nobunaga became equally enamored of that way and followed the same path?

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi was a gifted man who had wholly absorbed Nobunaga’s strengths and applied them with living ingenuity, and his power was now at its zenith; but if anyone else tried to imitate Nobunaga, the attempt was destined to end in tragedy. Mitsuhide’s raising of a rebel army had also been unconsciously influenced by Nobunaga, while Kawajiri Hizen-no-kami seemed to imagine himself another Nobunaga. It was proof of the powerful influence Nobunaga’s spirit exerted upon his subordinates.
